Calculate center of the area center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2 center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2 center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0]) mobject.scale(scale_factor) mobject.move_to(center) return mobject class Section6Scene(TeachingScene): def construct(self): # Euler identity part 1: e^(i*pi) = -1 (Issue 37: Position at E3, scale 0.9) # Using Text instead of MathTex to ensure reliability identity1 = Text("e^(i*pi)=-1", font_size=36) self.place_at_grid(identity1, 'E3', scale_factor=0.9) # Identity part 2: e^(i*pi) + 1 = 0 identity2 = Text("e^(i*pi)+1=0", font_size=36) self.place_at_grid(identity2, 'E3', scale_factor=0.9) # Setup colors for constants in identity2 # Indices: e:0, ^:1, (:2, i:3, *:4, p:5, i:6, ):7, +:8, 1:9, =:10, 0:11 identity2[0].set_color(BLUE) # e identity2[3].set_color(PINK) # i identity2[5:7].set_color(GOLD) # pi identity2[9].set_color(WHITE) # 1 identity2[11].set_color(GRAY) # 0 # Load asset: glowing ring (Issue 25) ring_asset_path = "/mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ring.svg" ring = SVGMobject(ring_asset_path, color=YELLOW) self.place_at_grid(ring, 'E3', scale_factor=1.8) # outline.topic: Euler's Formula: The Most Beautiful Connection in Mathematics
outline.target_audience: Advanced High School Students or First-Year University Students

sections.title: The Reunion of Five Great Constants
sections.content: Introduce the five most important numbers in mathematics: 0, 1, e, π, and i. Explain that while they seem unrelated (geometry, calculus, and algebra), Euler’s Identity brings them together in one simple equation. Use a character-driven hook to spark curiosity.
sections.example: A visual 'Gathering of Giants': Euler the Owl introduces 1 (the unit), 0 (the void), π (the circle), e (the growth), and i (the mystery).

sections.title: Prerequisite 1: The Power of 'i' as a Rotation
sections.content: Establish the foundation of the complex plane. Explain that multiplying a real number by 'i' isn't just an abstract concept; it represents a 90-degree counter-clockwise rotation on a 2D plane. Show the transition from a 1D number line to a 2D coordinate system.
sections.example: A compass needle pointing at 1. When multiplied by 'i', the needle rotates 90 degrees to point at the vertical 'i' axis.

sections.title: Prerequisite 2: Redefining Growth with 'e'
sections.content: Briefly revisit 'e' as the base of continuous growth. Normally, e^x represents growth along the real number line. Ask the key question: 'What happens if we grow in an imaginary direction (e^ix)?'
sections.example: A rocket representing e^x moving forward on a straight track. Now, imagine a steering wheel turning the rocket's thrust sideways by 90 degrees using 'i'.

sections.title: The Visual Derivation: Walking the Unit Circle
sections.content: Explain that e^(ix) describes a point moving along the circumference of a circle with a radius of 1. As 'x' (the angle in radians) increases, the point rotates. Introduce the general formula: e^(ix) = cos(x) + i sin(x).
sections.example: An ant walking along the edge of a circular clock. Its horizontal position is cos(x) and its vertical position is sin(x). At any angle 'x', its position is e^(ix).

sections.title: The Special Case: Reaching π
sections.content: Plug x = π into the formula. On the unit circle, an angle of π radians (180 degrees) lands the point exactly on the negative real axis. This demonstrates why e^(πi) results in -1.
sections.example: The ant walks halfway around the circle (distance π). It stops exactly at the number -1 on the horizontal axis. Visual: e^(πi) = -1.

sections.title: Summary and Elegance
sections.content: Final synthesis: Show the equation e^(πi) + 1 = 0. Summarize how growth (e) and rotation (i/π) combine to reach the simplest balance (0 and 1).
sections.example: A grand animation where the circle, the triangle (sin/cos), and the exponential curve merge into the single, elegant line of the identity.

storyboard.title: The Reunion of Five Great Constants
lecture_lines: Meet five legends of the mathematical world.
Unity and void: the numbers one and zero.
Transcendental stars: the constants e and pi.
The mysterious imaginary unit, i.
Together, they form the most beautiful equation.
animations: Fade in five mathematical constants: 0 (#CCCCCC), 1 (#FFFFFF), e (#00BFFF), \pi (#FFD700), and i (#FF69B4) at random positions.
Group 1 and 0 in the center and increase their scale to emphasize unity and void.
Bring e and \pi to the center, highlighting them with a soft glow to show their transcendental nature.
Bring i to the center, changing its color to a brighter pink (#FF1493) to show its unique role.
Smoothly transition all five constants into the equation e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0 in white (#FFFFFF).

storyboard.title: Prerequisite 1: The Power of 'i' as a Rotation
lecture_lines: We start on the standard real number line.
Multiplying by i rotates us ninety degrees.
This rotation defines the vertical imaginary axis.
animations: Draw a white horizontal line (#FFFFFF) with a small arrow pointing at the number 1.
Rotate the arrow 90 degrees counter-clockwise around the origin point (0).
Draw a pink vertical line (#FF69B4) intersecting the horizontal line, labeled 'i'.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite 2: Redefining Growth with 'e'
lecture_lines: The number e drives continuous exponential growth.
But i adds a twist to this expansion.
It steers growth sideways into the complex plane.
animations: Draw a blue vector (#00BFFF) representing e^x growing along a straight path.
Show a rotation symbol (arc) labeled 'i' appearing at the tip of the vector.
Shift the direction of the blue growth vector by 90 degrees to point upwards.

storyboard.title: The Visual Derivation: Walking the Unit Circle
lecture_lines: Imaginary growth traces a perfect unit circle.
Horizontal distance is captured by the cosine.
Vertical height is tracked by the sine.
As the angle grows, the point rotates.
This gives us the famous Euler’s formula.
animations: Create a gold circle (#FFD700) of radius 2 with a moving point on its edge.
Show a green horizontal line (#00FF00) tracking the point's distance from the center.
Show a red vertical line (#FF0000) tracking the point's height above the center.
Draw the angle x as an arc from the horizontal axis to the point.
Display the formula e^{ix} = \cos(x) + i \sin(x) at the top in white (#FFFFFF).

storyboard.title: The Special Case: Reaching π
lecture_lines: Rotate exactly halfway around, to an angle pi.
We land precisely at negative one.
Thus, e to the i pi equals negative one.
animations: Animate the point moving along the gold circle arc from 0 to \pi radians.
Highlight the moment the point reaches the negative real axis at -1.
Replace the moving point with the text 'e^{i\pi} = -1' in white (#FFFFFF).

storyboard.title: Summary and Elegance
lecture_lines: Simply add one to return to zero.
Five fundamental constants are now perfectly united.
A single ring binds this mathematical masterpiece.
Witness the ultimate elegance of Euler's identity.
Simple, profound, and absolutely beautiful.
animations: Transform the expression e^{i\pi} = -1 into e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0 at the center.
Cycle through the colors of each constant: e (blue), i (pink), \pi (gold), 1 (white), 0 (gray).
Draw a glowing ring [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ring.svg] around the entire identity e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0.
Scale up the entire equation until it fills the screen, then scale back down.
Slowly fade out everything except the white text of the identity.
